key_concept: In a non-magnetic dielectric the wave speed is $v = c/\sqrt{\epsilon_r}$, the wavelength is $\lambda = v/f$, and the field amplitudes are linked by $B_0 = E_0/v$ (not $B_0/v$), with $\vec E \times \vec B$ pointing along the direction of propagation.
steps: Speed: assume a non-magnetic medium, so $\mu_r = 1$. Then $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_r}} = \dfrac{3\times10^8}{\sqrt{9}} = 10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Statement (1) is correct.
Frequency: compare with $\sin(kz - \omega t)$. This gives $\omega = 2\pi\times10^6\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$, so $f = 10^6\ \text{Hz}$.
Wavelength in the medium: $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{10^8}{10^6} = 100\ \text{m}$. The value 300 m is the free-space wavelength $c/f$, so statement (2) is incorrect.
Magnetic field direction: $\vec E$ is along $\hat x$ and propagation is along $+\hat z$. Since $\hat x \times \hat y = \hat z$, $\vec B$ must lie along $+\hat y$ and be in phase with $\vec E$.
Magnetic field magnitude: in the medium $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{v}$. So the correct relation is $B_y = \dfrac{E_0}{v}\sin(kz - 2\pi\times10^6 t)$.
The given form $B_y = \dfrac{B_0}{v}\sin(\ldots)$ divides a magnetic amplitude by a speed. Its unit is $\text{T s m}^{-1}$, which is not a magnetic field, so statement (3) is incorrect.
Direction of propagation: the phase $(kz - \omega t)$ stays constant only if $z$ increases with $t$, so the wave moves along $+z$. Statement (4) is correct.
Hence statements (2) and (3) are both incorrect, which is why NTA accepted both options.
final_answer: Option (2): The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is 300 m; and Option (3): The magnetic field is given by the relation $B_y = \frac{B_0}{v}\sin(kz - 2\pi\times10^6 t)$ (both accepted)
why_not_others: Option (1) is a correct statement because $v = c/\sqrt{9} = 10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Option (4) is correct because the phase $(kz - \omega t)$ describes a wave moving along $+z$. Neither can be the 'incorrect choice'.
common_trap: Students calculate $\lambda = c/f = 300\ \text{m}$ using the vacuum speed, forgetting that the speed, and hence the wavelength, drop by a factor of $\sqrt{\epsilon_r} = 3$ inside the dielectric, while the frequency stays the same.
time_saving_tip: Remember that $\lambda_{\text{medium}} = \lambda_0/n$ with $n = \sqrt{\epsilon_r} = 3$, giving $300/3 = 100\ \text{m}$ instantly. A quick unit check ($B_0/v$ is not in tesla) rules out (3) without further work.
